findings.summary: sync-command.ts at 600 lines is a procedural orchestrator with multiple responsibilities (config loading, lifecycle, file sync, settings, reporting)
evidence: processSingleRepo, runLifecyclePhase, runFileSyncPhase, applyRepoSettings, displayReports are all top-level functions in a single file doing orchestration at different levels
RepoIterationContext has 13 fields bundling unrelated concerns (processor, lifecycleManager, tokenManager, settingsCollector, three factory types)
findings.suggestion: Extract lifecycle, settings application, and reporting into separate orchestrator classes or modules to localize change

findings.summary: pr-creator.ts mixes template formatting, PR creation orchestration, and merge orchestration in a single file with module-level functions
evidence: formatPRBody, formatPRTitle, loadDefaultTemplate, createPR, and mergePR are all exported from the same file
createPR internally constructs a PRWorkflowExecutor and calls it — thin wrapper that could be eliminated
findings.suggestion: Separate PR body/title formatting into a dedicated formatter module; consider whether createPR/mergePR wrappers add value over direct PRWorkflowExecutor usage

findings.summary: Large options objects are passed through multiple layers with overlapping fields, creating glue-code entropy
evidence: CommitPushOptions has 11 fields (repoInfo, gitOps, workDir, fileChanges, commitMessage, pushBranch, isDirectMode, dryRun, retries, token, executor)
BranchSetupOptions has 10 fields with significant overlap with CommitPushOptions (repoInfo, workDir, dryRun, retries, token, executor)
SyncWorkflow.execute destructures ProcessorOptions then rebuilds similar bags for branchManager.setupBranch and commitPushManager.commitAndPush
findings.suggestion: Introduce a shared session/context type that carries the common fields (repoInfo, workDir, dryRun, retries, token, executor) once, with operation-specific types adding only unique fields

findings.summary: GitHub token resolution happens in two places: sync-command resolves it for lifecycle/settings, and AuthOptionsBuilder resolves it again for file sync
evidence: sync-command.ts line 340-349: resolveGitHubToken called and result passed as repoToken
auth-options-builder.ts line 29-35: resolveGitHubToken called again when preResolvedToken is undefined
The preResolvedToken path in AuthOptionsBuilder exists solely to handle the fact that sync-command already resolved the token
findings.suggestion: Resolve token once in the outer loop and pass it through consistently, or let AuthOptionsBuilder be the sole resolver

findings.summary: AuthOptionsBuilder accesses process.env.GH_TOKEN directly, violating the codebase's own DI principle for shared/library code
evidence: auth-options-builder.ts line 35: process.env.GH_TOKEN passed directly to resolveGitHubToken
CLAUDE.md states: 'src/shared/ and src/sync/ modules must not import global singletons. Pass them in.'
findings.suggestion: Accept the environment token as a constructor parameter or resolve option rather than reading process.env directly

findings.summary: CommitPushManager calls getCommitStrategy (selecting between Git and GraphQL) based on repo type, but this selection logic is spread across sync-command and commit-push-manager
evidence: sync-command.ts line 488: isGraphQLCommitMode computed as isGitHubRepo(repoInfo) && ctx.tokenManager !== null
commit-push-manager.ts line 49: getCommitStrategy(repoInfo, executor) called without isGraphQLCommitMode context — the strategy factory makes its own determination
isGraphQLCommitMode is threaded through ProcessorOptions -> FileWriteContext but not used by CommitPushManager
findings.suggestion: Centralize commit strategy selection in one place — either the factory handles all selection logic, or the caller decides and injects the strategy

findings.summary: Config validator has repetitive validation patterns that could be extracted into a small validation DSL or helper
evidence: validateFileConfigFields manually checks booleanFields with for-of loop (lines 99-114), stringFields with identical loop (lines 116-126), then separate header and vars checks
validateRawConfig has duplicated hasGroupFiles/hasGroupSettings logic that's repeated in validateForSync (lines 659-688 vs 723-757)
findings.suggestion: Extract a fieldValidator helper that takes field name, expected type, and context; extract the hasGroupFiles/hasGroupSettings checks into shared predicates

findings.summary: GraphQL response parsing uses chains of unsafe type casts instead of a typed parser or schema validation
evidence: Lines 282-289: const data = parsed.data as Record<string, unknown> | undefined; const commit = (data?.createCommitOnBranch as Record<string, unknown> | undefined)?.commit as Record<string, unknown> | undefined; const oid = commit?.oid as string | undefined;
Lines 480-491: similar casting chain for queryRemoteRef response
findings.suggestion: Define typed response interfaces and use a small type guard or assertion function to validate the response shape once

findings.summary: LabelsProcessor manually rebuilds update payload from propertyChanges array instead of using a more direct mapping
evidence: Lines 114-127: constructs updatePayload by looping over propertyChanges and checking prop.property against string literals ('color', 'description', 'new_name') with individual if branches
findings.suggestion: Use Object.fromEntries or a reduce to map propertyChanges directly to the payload shape

findings.summary: FileWriter iterates over files twice — once for content writing and once for executable permissions
evidence: Lines 57-135: first loop writes files and tracks changes
Lines 137-154: second loop over same files array checks shouldBeExecutable
The second loop re-checks fileChanges.get(file.fileName) which was set in the first loop
findings.suggestion: Handle executable permissions in the first loop after writing, or collect executable files during the first pass for a targeted second pass
